text: It was a three-day festival and on the second night I took what I was told was one tab of LSD, but I think it was much stronger than that, maybe 300 or more. For the first hour it was amazing, the lights on the main stage were melting into the crowd and I was dancing with my friends. Then I went to get water and when I came back I couldn't find them. Everyone looked the same, faces kept changing, and I started to panic. I walked for what felt like hours and kept ending up at the same food truck. I became convinced I was stuck in a loop, that time had stopped and that I had actually died and this was some kind of purgatory where I would wander forever. I remember sitting on the ground and screaming. Some security people found me and took me to the medical tent. I couldn't tell them my name. They gave me something to calm me down and I lay there under a foil blanket until morning. A volunteer sat next to me the whole time and kept telling me I was safe, which I didn't believe until the sun came up. My friends found me around 7am.

Ich habe allein in meiner Wohnung Pilze genommen, ca. 3 Gramm. Nach einer halben Stunde bekam ich starkes Herzrasen und war überzeugt, dass ich einen Herzinfarkt habe. Ich habe mich nicht getraut, jemanden anzurufen, weil ich Angst vor der Polizei hatte. Ich lag stundenlang auf dem Badezimmerboden und dachte, ich sterbe jetzt. Irgendwann ließ es nach, aber ich war völlig fertig.

I went to a retreat center in the Peruvian Amazon for a 10-day ayahuasca retreat. I had done a lot of reading and I thought I was well prepared. The first two ceremonies were mostly physical, a lot of purging and some beautiful visions of jungle animals and geometric patterns. The third ceremony was different. About 40 minutes after drinking I felt a presence enter the maloca, something very dark and old. At first I thought it was part of the cleansing the shaman had talked about. But it came closer and I felt it was looking at me, and it knew everything about me. I saw images of every terrible thing I had ever done or thought, and the entity was laughing. I tried to call for help but I couldn't move or speak. I felt my body dissolving and then there was no body anymore, just me as a small point of awareness in an endless black space with this thing.

I don't know how long it lasted. In the ayahuasca world it felt like years. I tried to remember my name, my mother's face, anything, and nothing was there. The worst was that I understood, with total certainty, that this was the truth of reality, and that my normal life had been a thin illusion over this void.

At some point I came back to the room. I was lying in my own vomit and I was shaking violently. I saw the shaman was singing at the other end of the maloca but nobody came to me. One of the facilitators finally sat with me but she seemed nervous and told me to 'surrender to the medicine'. I couldn't surrender, there was nothing to surrender to, I was terrified that if I closed my eyes I would go back there. The singing felt like it was mocking me.

When the ceremony ended I walked to my hut and sat awake until morning. The next day I told the organisers I wanted to leave and they tried to convince me to stay and do another ceremony to 'finish the process'. I left anyway and took a boat to Iquitos and then flew home a week early. Throughout the journey I felt like I was watching myself from outside, like a ghost following a body around. On the plane I had a panic attack and the flight attendant brought me oxygen. I didn't feel like a person for a long time after that.
Bad trip on mushrooms, I thought I was going insane and would never come back to normal.

Ich war auf einer Technoparty und habe LSD genommen. Später hat mir jemand noch Ketamin angeboten, und ich habe ohne nachzudenken eine Line gezogen. Das war ein riesiger Fehler. Plötzlich war mein Körper weg, ich konnte meine Arme und Beine nicht mehr spüren, und die Musik wurde zu einem einzigen Dröhnen. Ich hatte das Gefühl, in eine Art Tunnel gezogen zu werden, und dass ich da nicht mehr rauskomme. Die Zeit hat sich wiederholt, immer und immer wieder dieselbe Sekunde. Ich habe versucht, meinen Freunden etwas zu sagen, aber ich wusste nicht mehr, wie Sprechen geht. Irgendwann saß ich draußen an der Wand, eine Freundin hat meine Hand gehalten. Ich wusste nicht, ob sie echt ist. Das ging so etwa zwei Stunden, danach kam ich langsam zurück, aber die Welt sah noch lange seltsam flach und künstlich aus.

I smoked DMT with a friend who had done it a few times. I took three big hits and broke through almost immediately. I was in a room made of moving patterns, very bright, and there were beings there. At first they seemed curious, then I felt they were angry that I was there. They started doing something to me, like taking me apart and examining the pieces. I felt them inside my head. I had no body, no name, I didn't know I had taken a drug. I was absolutely certain this was death and that these beings were going to keep me. I could hear a kind of high-pitched mechanical laughter.
When I came back after about 10-15 minutes, my heart was racing so fast that I thought I was having a cardiac arrest. My friend said I was screaming and that I tried to get up and run. I couldn't stop shaking for an hour. I kept asking him if I was real and if he was real. He was scared too, he didn't know what to do. I didn't sleep that night and I was afraid to close my eyes in case they came back. For days I felt like they could still see me.

I took 5-MeO-DMT at a retreat with a facilitator. I'd been told it would be a beautiful experience of oneness. The moment I inhaled, everything vanished. Not just me, everything. There was no up or down, no time, no me. Just a white roar. Then I came back, and the first thing I knew was that I was screaming. I didn't know what I was or where I was. It felt like being born into a body that wasn't mine. The facilitator was holding me and I was clawing at her arms. It took about 20 minutes before I could understand words. She said this happens sometimes. I didn't feel unity or love, just total annihilation.

Ich war mit drei Freunden in einem Ferienhaus, wir hatten Pilztee getrunken. Am Anfang war alles lustig, dann fing ich an, die Gespräche der anderen merkwürdig zu finden. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass sie über mich reden und sich über mich lustig machen. Jeder Blick, jedes Lachen schien gegen mich gerichtet zu sein. Ich wurde immer misstrauischer und war mir irgendwann sicher, dass sie mir etwas ins Getränk getan hatten und mich loswerden wollten. Ich bin aus dem Haus gerannt, barfuß, mitten in der Nacht, und in den Wald gelaufen. Ich habe mich hinter einem Baum versteckt und gezittert, ich hörte Stimmen, die meinen Namen gerufen haben, und dachte, sie suchen mich, um mir etwas anzutun. Es war kalt und dunkel, ich hatte überall Kratzer an den Füßen. Irgendwann kam ein Auto, und es war die Polizei, weil meine Freunde sie gerufen hatten. Ich habe mich gewehrt, weil ich dachte, die Polizisten gehören auch dazu. Sie haben mich ins Krankenhaus gebracht, wo ich die Nacht verbracht habe. Am nächsten Tag habe ich mich unglaublich geschämt. Die Freundschaft zu zweien von den dreien ist danach zerbrochen, weil ich mich nicht mehr in ihre Nähe getraut habe.

Smoked salvia at a party. For maybe 5 minutes I became a chair in a kitchen in another world. I forgot I was ever human. When I came back I was terrified that I would be a chair again. Short but horrible.

This is hard to write about but I'll try to be thorough. I was 22 at the time, in my last year of university. I'd taken LSD maybe six or seven times before and always had good experiences, usually with friends in a park or at home with music. This time I decided to take a higher dose alone, because I had been reading about people having profound spiritual experiences at higher doses and I wanted that. I took what I believed to be 400ug in my room on a Saturday afternoon.

For the first two hours it was intense but manageable. Strong visuals, a lot of emotion, I cried about my grandmother who died the year before. Then around the peak, something shifted. I started to have thoughts that felt like they were coming from outside me. Messages. I became convinced that I had been chosen to understand the secret structure of reality, and that everything in my life had been arranged to lead me to this moment. The numbers on my alarm clock meant something, the pattern of the curtains meant something, the songs on the radio were speaking directly to me. At first this felt amazing, like enlightenment.

Then it turned. I realised (in the trip logic) that if I was the one who understood, I was also responsible. That the fate of everyone depended on me making the right decisions in the next few minutes. I started to feel that the world would end if I made a mistake. I couldn't figure out what the right decision was. Every choice seemed to lead to catastrophe. I was pacing around my room, opening and closing the window, turning the lights on and off, trying to find the correct sequence. I was sobbing and talking to myself.

My flatmate came home around 9pm and found me sitting naked in the bathtub with the water running cold, repeating that I had to stay still or everyone would die. He tried to talk to me but I thought he was a test, and that if I responded wrongly it would be over. He called an ambulance.

I don't remember the ambulance ride clearly. At the hospital they gave me a sedative. I slept for a long time. When I woke up the next day I was still not right. The acid had worn off but the thoughts hadn't. I still felt the messages, still felt chosen and responsible. The doctors said it was a drug-induced psychosis. I was kept for observation for five days and then transferred to a psychiatric ward for another two weeks. During that time I was very confused, sometimes I knew it was the drug, sometimes I was sure it was real and they were keeping me from my mission. I was terrified of the other patients and of the nurses. My parents came from another city and I didn't trust them either at first.

The acute LSD part was maybe 10 hours, but the experience that I'd call traumatic lasted around three weeks, and the worst part was not knowing if I'd ever be normal again.

Ich hatte eine sehr schwierige Erfahrung mit LSD, bei der ich das Gefühl hatte, mich komplett aufzulösen. Ich wusste nicht mehr, wer ich bin, und hatte das Gefühl, dass es mich nie gegeben hat. Das war schlimmer als jede Angst, die ich kannte.
Horrortrip auf Pilzen mit Herzrasen und Todesangst.
